axes.note: figure axes are (detection, excitation); our convention is (omega_tau, omega_t) = (excitation, detection)

map_type: SIGNED (diverging red/blue colormap, white = zero) -- this is a real-part or in-phase map, NOT a magnitude map. Model |FFT| censuses are not directly comparable without taking the same component.
digitisation_method: visual, by eye, from the supplied raster; positions +-0.05 THz, amplitudes are a 5-level ordinal scale (3 = strongest observed)
structural_observations: The map is dominated by the excitation rows at +-0.38 THz (qFM) and 0, NOT by rows at 0.50 THz (E12).

Along each strong row the sign alternates (-,+,-,+) with roughly 0.3 THz spacing, which is the signature of dispersive real-part lineshapes rather than of separate peaks; a magnitude map would merge these.
The two features singled out with + markers lie on the qAFM excitation row (0.90) at detection 0.50 and 1.25 -- i.e. (qAFM, E12) and (qAFM, E13) in our convention.
No strong feature is visible on an excitation row at 0.50 THz (E12).
Detection extends to 2 THz with no feature beyond ~1.3 THz.

discrepancy_flag.issue: This differs from the same-polarised list used to build the current model, which was (omega_tau, omega_t) = (0.5,0), (0.5,0.7), (0.5,1.2), (0.9,0.38), (0.9,1.2) with the 0.5-excitation family strongest.
discrepancy_flag.as_read_here: the 0.9-excitation family is what is marked, and the dominant unmarked structure is at excitation 0.38 and 0
discrepancy_flag.needs_confirmation: whether the earlier list used (detection, excitation) ordering rather than (excitation, detection), which would map (0.5,0.7)->(0.7,0.5) etc.
